finding: 552 retained differential detections; the 1930s event survives quality/control checks, with a photographic event/baseline contrast near +0.68 mag.
meaning: A real historical multiyear fade is supported.
limit: Only three points sample 1892-1893; photographic and modern passbands differ. A nondetection is not zero flux.
independence: DASCH plate exposures; control/reduction variants reuse them.

finding: Catalogue photometry, native pixels, calibration controls and scanner orientations were checked without a dependable independent reproduction of the dimming.
meaning: The checks expose real calibration/scanner limitations.
limit: Two scans of the same glass share one exposure. Natural photographic response and calibration controls remain material.
independence: Separate archive from DASCH; x/y scans of one plate are not independent.

finding: Same-frame ensemble correction gives about +0.147 mag fading 2004-2007 and -0.114 mag recovery by 2009; leaving out individual controls retains the fading.
meaning: An intermediate fading/recovery episode fills part of the historical gap.
limit: Another episode does not establish a fixed period or identical eclipse geometry.
independence: ASAS observations are distinct from ASAS-SN.

finding: 470 accepted target points and 364 same-exposure differential measurements; +0.3089 mag fading to 2022 and -0.1393 mag recovery to 2025.
meaning: Comparison-corrected modern optical fading and recovery.
limit: The saved target data contain g only; no validated ZTF g-r curve was obtained.
independence: ZTF exposures; rotation/color/model tests reuse them.

finding: 5,249 rows retrieved;5,180 accepted V/g exposures. Separate g cameras give +0.285 to +0.313 mag fading 2018-2022 and support recovery continuing into 2026.
meaning: Independent optical replication of the modern fade.
limit: Cameras/passbands retain separate zero points; no V at the 2022 minimum. Camera-days can share an observing night.
independence: Independent of ZTF; repeat fits are not extra observations.

finding: Comparison-corrected visit medians fade about +0.1163 mag in W1 and +0.0894 mag in W2, then partly recover. Matched 2018/2022 contrasts are +0.1175/+0.08875 mag.
meaning: The infrared dims less than optical g.
limit: W1/W2 are bands of one instrument. Calibration, molecular absorption and visit matching matter.
independence: WISE/NEOWISE is distinct from optical surveys; both bands share visits.

finding: g-W1 reddens roughly 0.19-0.22 mag. The 2017/18 V/g rotation amplitudes agree within uncertainty; half-day cross-band matches cover only 30 distinct V dates.
meaning: Wavelength-dependent fading and a second-band rotation check.
limit: No reliable temperature-specific V-g variation or hysteresis. Several mechanisms fit the same endpoint colors.
independence: Derived from E04-E06, not an additional instrument.

finding: Allowing seasonal phase/amplitude evolution gives peaks near 35.78 days (ASAS-SN) and 36.30 days (ZTF). Annual aliases fit worse across most seasons.
meaning: A recurring roughly 36-day photometric clock compatible with rotation.
limit: Peak widths are not formal period errors. A 71.84-day rotation with two active longitudes remains possible. Photometry is not an orbital RV measurement.
independence: Two surveys, reusing E04/E05 for another feature.

finding: No simple seasonal amplitude-versus-brightness trend. Stronger early 2024/25 modulation is hidden by the weak season-long fit; later amplitude/phase changes differ.
meaning: Evolving surface patterns remain compatible with the clock.
limit: Rotation amplitude measures asymmetry, not total spot area. No spot lifetime, differential rotation or simple activity-cycle law is measured.
independence: Further analyses of E04/E05.

finding: The 912.3-day waveform fails modern replay/forward tests. Holding one exact 35.92-day waveform fixed across years also worsens later predictions.
meaning: Neither stable waveform describes the modern observations.
limit: This does not reject a recurring rotation timescale with evolving spots or establish a replacement long period.
independence: Tests of models on the same optical observations.

finding: Episodes have unequal depths and incomplete coverage. Tested equal-depth repeats fail; a post-hoc approximately 15-year schedule has covered misses and large gaps.
meaning: Repeated multiyear fading, without an established regular cycle.
limit: The 1930 s-to-2020s gap is not a measured 88-year orbit. An approximately 7.96-year historical gap remains unfilled.
independence: Derived from E01/E03-E05.

finding: P=35.9205+/-0.0306 days, K1=10.72+/-0.81 km/s, 21 good velocities and eccentricity consistent with zero. The period approximately matches the optical clock.
meaning: A concrete close-companion candidate and plausible tidal-activity connection.
limit: Efficiency/significance fall below recommended gold-sample thresholds. Epoch RVs were unavailable for refitting; binary classification/synchronization remain unconfirmed.
independence: Gaia spectroscopy is independent of the optical light curves.

finding: Reported SB1 parameters imply f (M)=0.0045872 solar masses. For a 1.5-solar-mass primary, example companions are 0.240/0.282/0.533 solar masses at inclinations 90/60/30 degrees.
meaning: A low-mass dynamically relevant companion and tidal maintenance of activity are physically compatible.
limit: Mass, inclination, envelope properties and tidal prescription are assumptions, not an observed companion mass or proof of locking.
independence: Theory applied to E12, not another detector.

finding: Gaia-based luminosity 54.64 solar luminosities and temperature~5206 K contrast with a literature~4500 K atmosphere/low poster gravity. Conditional radii near 9-12 solar radii contrast with a substantially larger low-gravity solution.
meaning: The object is treated as a giant; a consistent atmosphere/radius solution needs improvement.
limit: No seismic radius or measured flare temperature. Tidal and energy calculations inherit the stellar-parameter uncertainty.
independence: Catalogue/literature estimates; downstream calculations share them.

dataset: Published Ca II H/K and FAST, 2008-2012
finding: Tang et al. reported chromospheric Ca II H/K emission. Ten FAST spectra show weaker H-alpha absorption on 12 November 2009 than October 2008: 0.480+/-0.085 Angstrom formal-noise contrast.
meaning: Chromospheric activity; H-alpha variability compatible with core fill-in.
limit: About 1.675% differential continuum bias can reproduce the H-alpha contrast. This is not a flare precursor or proof of a shared episode with Swift 20 days later.
independence: FAST observations and published spectroscopy; repeated reductions reuse spectra.

finding: No convincing detached blueshifted H-alpha absorption. Broad Mg/Na indices supply no precise temperature change.
meaning: No spectroscopic identification of erupting gas or measured cooling.
limit: Sparse spectra/resolution do not exclude all mass loss or spots. Lack of blueshift is not a detection of obstruction.
independence: Same FAST observations as E15.

finding: Synthetic 10 km/s shifts are recovered numerically, but same-night repeat shifts differ by 20-24 km/s and separate line windows disagree. Sky/telluric checks do not solve this.
meaning: Existing extracted spectra cannot independently test the candidate 10.72 km/s semi-amplitude.
limit: Numerical shift recovery is not calibrated RV precision. The cleaner 2010 pair does not establish an orbit.
independence: Same FAST spectra as E15/E16.

dataset: Six calibrated pixel intervals; four excursions
finding: Four positive compact excursions: 16/22 November 2021, 23 December 2021, 28 November 2023. Common model FWHM~6.34/6.24/5.38/4.80 hours; December 23 remains largest.
meaning: Repeated hour-scale brightening strengthens activity; November 22/December 23 have the clearest fast-rise/slow-decay shapes.
limit: November 16 is nearly symmetric and less flare-specific. November 16/November 28 have large baseline envelopes. Selection was exploratory, not a blind false-alarm experiment.
independence: One TESS instrument across separate dates. QLP/SPOC/custom apertures reuse photons.

finding: Model ED 231/286/809/243 seconds; baseline/aperture envelopes 219-452/268-302/809-961/237-483 seconds. Nominal face-on patch energies 2.04e37/2.52e37/7.13e37/2.14e37 erg.
meaning: If stellar flares associated with this system, all are superflare-scale under the common assumptions.
limit: Isotropic energies are four times face-on values. Luminosity, flare spectrum, geometry, dilution and component attribution are assumed. Radiation is not kinetic/magnetic energy; conditional bootstrap errors omit baseline systematics.
independence: Models of E18, not an independent energy observation.

finding: 80 matched controls/event calibrate template offsets. Apparent hourly drift is unusual for November 22/December 23. Pointing-gradient terms change mean flux amplitudes by<0.3% relative; hourly changes<0.9%.
meaning: The tested pointing terms do not remove the excess; pixel positions add information beyond an aperture curve.
limit: Stationary astrometry is not established. December 23 is marginally outside its noise-only radius; November 28 is less precise. No official PRF/attitude or full moving-object exclusion; close components remain unresolved.
independence: Same TESS pixels as E18. Controls match actual counts/timestamp patterns.

finding: Direct pixels retain 114.51 nominal cadence-days versus 104.18 days for the earlier light-curve union. New 1152 profile injections give effective search times 93.33/108.47/113.90/111.25 days. Earlier 1296 injections remain separate.
meaning: Sensitivity to representative shapes and gaps is quantified; original-sized sampled events are usually recoverable.
limit: Quality rules explain the coverage difference; neither is live-time. Effective exposure is profile-specific. Four candidates do not establish a flare-frequency distribution or magnetic-cycle dependence.
independence: Synthetic tests of E18 exposures, not new observations.

finding: No stable repeating eclipse. Tested 3%-deep 1-6 day profiles are recovered across selected injection phases; weaker limits depend on baseline/reduction.
meaning: Persistent deep eclipses of the tested shapes are disfavored.
limit: Noneclipsing companions, dilution, grazing geometry and upstream attenuation remain possible. No universal depth upper limit.
independence: Same TESS exposures, tested at longer timescales.

finding: No reproducible localized oscillation envelope at 10-200 microHz. Retaining the December flare raises sector 46 power at 30-100 microHz by 1.88 (SAP)/3.04 (corrected).
meaning: Transient contamination matters; no usable seismic mass/radius.
limit: The lower-gravity prediction near 6 microHz was outside the search. No intrinsically nonoscillating-star or binary classification follows.
independence: Same TESS light curves; signal-removal variants are not independent.

finding: 2SXPS J075445.6+164139: 18 counts/4183s, offset 3.88 arcsec inside 5.6 arcsec 90%radius. Conditional thermal-plasma conversion gives Lx~4.2e31 erg/s at 1668 pc.
meaning: An archival X-ray source associated with the position supports an active corona in the system.
limit: Two useful snapshot bins do not resolve a flare (constancy p~.141). This is 12 years before the 2021 TESS event; a FAST visit 20 days earlier does not identify a shared episode.
independence: Swift XRT is independent of TESS/eROSITA. UVOT is another detector on Swift.

finding: 3eRASS J075445.3+164136: 23.60+/-5.89 net counts; 0.2-2.3 keV catalogue flux~9.04e-14 erg/s/cm2. Exact Gaia 667401913089980544 selected: p_any=.918834, p_i=.99999994, match_flag 1.
meaning: Independent X-ray survey strongly favors association with J 0754 among Gaia candidates.
limit: p_i is conditional within Gaia. A faint nearby UVOT object is outside that comparison. Catalogue-only DR2 cannot resolve a flare; DR1/DR2 overlap. Different Swift/eROSITA bands cannot directly establish flux variability.
independence: Independent of Swift; DR1/DR2 are not two instruments or disjoint exposures.

finding: NUV AB 18.614+/-0.053 match at 0.142 arcsec. Two short runs span 97/82 nominal seconds. Corrected background/flat/sensitivity/deadtime fluctuations remain weak and strongly bin dependent.
meaning: NUV emission is measured; no convincing new UV flare.
limit: Coverage cannot characterize hours-long flares. No reliable FUV numerical limit or temperature/rotation-specific NUV excess is established by these timing tests.
independence: GALEX is separate; its catalogue/photon reductions share exposures.

finding: First image crosses an exposure edge (central pixel~8.44 s); second has uniform 2390 scoverage. Their apparent count difference cannot be treated as variability.
meaning: A real exposure problem explains a misleading comparison.
limit: No UVOT flare or calibrated two-snapshot variability. Coincidence loss, aperture correction and the cool-star optical red leak matter for absolute UV inference.
independence: UVOT differs from XRT. These images are not extra TESS flare candidates.

finding: No significant detection: forced flux-0.241+/-0.144,+0.108+/-0.146,-0.127+/-0.127 mJy. Approximate 3 sigma image bounds 0.432/0.545/0.382 mJy; no epoch change (p~.219).
meaning: Three radio visits supply image-level limits.
limit: No radio flare or brightness-change detection. Sparse nondetections do not exclude fainter emission or bursts between visits.
independence: One VLA instrument at three dates; Quick Look calibration/image-noise limits apply.

dataset: SPHEREx 2025/2026 and Gaia XP mean spectrum
finding: 223 SPHERExoverlaps yield 182 retained local measurements. Official/native extraction broadly agrees. A giant photosphere explains most flux; a~9%long-wave residual depends on model/calibration.
meaning: No dominant warm infrared emitter is required in the recovery-era spectra.
limit: No SPHEREx spectrum of the 2022 minimum. Native/local reductions share pixels; XP averages epochs. Cold dust or a small excess remains possible.
independence: SPHEREx/Gaia are separate; two SPHEREx reductions are not two observations.

finding: Atmosphere-nuisance CO/reference ranges include unity. Giant-only spectra pass the exploratory 5%shape allowance; adding a second spectrum improves residuals but is not required.
meaning: No robust CO emission, dust emission feature or luminous secondary is identified.
limit: Tolerance is not a confidence threshold. Similar-color components are normalization-degenerate; there is no useful general companion-light upper bound.
independence: Models reusing E29, not additional spectral detections.

finding: An illustrative 5000 Kphotosphere/~3650 Kspots changes projected coverage 30%to 49.6%; g/W1 fit predicts W2~0.0995 mag versus 0.08875 observed, inside the adopted 0.02 mag allowance.
meaning: Cool spots can reproduce the wavelength dependence and fit the activity picture.
limit: Spot temperature/coverage are example solutions, not measured surface properties. Compatibility does not prove that spots cause the whole fade.
independence: Theory applied to E04-E07, not independent confirmation.

finding: Tested ordinary uniform screens fail the optical/IR changes. Partial-covering/flatter-extinction families and some mixtures survive; the full trajectory does not decisively rank them.
meaning: Simple uniform attenuation is disfavored; nonuniform obscuration remains a comparison to spots.
limit: Rejection of one screen is not rejection of all dust. Passing a tolerance is not a posterior probability or detection of a disk.
independence: Competing models of the same data used in E31.

finding: Conditional opacity/geometry calculations explore material covering a giant for years. No cloud is measured, and no unique orbit/confinement mechanism is fitted.
meaning: A physical possibility was explored, not detected.
limit: Opacity, mass, expansion and confinement are assumptions. The H-alpha check supplies no detached blueshifted cloud detection.
independence: Illustrative theory using E14/E16, not an observed ejection.

finding: LAMOST repeats a failed/SNR-zero 2018 visit. Public APOGEE DR17/DR19 target queries are empty. Tested Hectochelle/old-Echelle routes add no suitable spectrum; the high-resolution poster spectrum remains unrecovered.
meaning: No new calibrated high-resolution RV/activity spectrum through these routes.
limit: Empty catalogues/restricted releases are bounded access results, not proof observations never existed. New high-resolution spectroscopy remains valuable.
independence: Separate searches with no additional spectrum to count.

finding: Tested 5 XMM/slew/CSCsource cones are empty. Nearby pointings do not establish useful target exposure.
meaning: No further source detection or useful target light curve recovered.
limit: Catalogue/pointing results are not measured X-ray flux upper limits and cannot establish fading between missions.
independence: Separate facilities with no positive target evidence to count.

finding: Pan-STARRS data are dominated by saturation/other flags; reported mean colors are not validated. Other optical/history routes retain sparse/flagged/unrecovered products rather than a new trustworthy color curve.
meaning: No extra validated optical color history or newly filled historical gap claimed.
limit: Sentinel/synthetic values cannot enter physical fits. Diagnostic candidates remain leads, not completed detections.
independence: Distinct archives with insufficient usable data in completed checks.
